_README: Every {{PLACEHOLDER}} in paper.md is resolved from here at build time.
An unresolved placeholder FAILS the build (see build.py). Never type a
number into the prose. `python3 build.py --draft` renders the gaps in red
instead of failing, so the paper can still be read while data lands.
value from JSON : {"file": <path from repo root>, "path": <dotted or list>,
LaTeX fragment  : {"tex_file": <path from repo root>}  (inserted verbatim)
fixed string    : {"literal": <string or null>}  (null = author must fill in)
gloss modes: "x_in_n" turns a percentage into plain English ("about four in
every five"); "fraction_word" turns a 0-1 ratio into "about a quarter".
`needs` on every entry says what the producing script must write. Four keys
do not exist yet and are flagged NOT YET PRODUCED.

N_MODELS.needs: number of distinct ranking models in the audit, after dropping the byte-identical semantic-ranker-default-003 (REVIEW_TODO A1)

N_MODELS_STEREOTYPE_ORDER.needs: how many models order male-typed above female-typed jobs, i.e. have a positive stereotype-tracking spread (REVIEW_TODO A3)

N_OCCUPATIONS.needs: occupations surviving the BLS labelling (REVIEW_TODO A8)

N_OCC_MALE.needs: occupations labelled male-typed by BLS share of women

N_OCC_FEMALE.needs: occupations labelled female-typed by BLS share of women

N_OCC_NEUTRAL.needs: occupations labelled evenly split by BLS share of women

N_PAIRS.needs: twin comparisons scored per model, after label filtering

N_TEMPLATES.needs: number of document templates (counted from the by_template breakdown)

N_QUERIES.needs: number of query phrasings (counted from the by_query_type breakdown)

N_NAME_PAIRS.needs: number of male/female name pairs (counted from the by_name_pair breakdown)

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS.needs: NOT YET PRODUCED. Median across models of the share of twin comparisons favoring the man on MALE-typed jobs. Add an `across_models` block to analyze_single_stage.py shaped exactly like the existing `neutral_across_models`, but for all three categories.

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS; generated automatically, same source value

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_FEMALEJOBS.needs: NOT YET PRODUCED. Median across models of the share favoring the man on FEMALE-typed jobs. Same `across_models` block as above.

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_NEUTRAL.needs: median across models of the share favoring the man on evenly split jobs (REVIEW_TODO A3: report the median, not the outlier-driven mean)

MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_NEUTRAL_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of MEDIAN_PCT_MALE_NEUTRAL; generated automatically

N_MODELS_NEUTRAL_LEAN_MALE.needs: models leaning toward men on evenly split jobs

N_MODELS_NEUTRAL_LEAN_FEMALE.needs: models leaning toward women on evenly split jobs

SLATE_SIZE.needs: NOT YET PRODUCED. Number of candidate documents in one simulated pool (half male-named, half female-named). Write the constant into the results JSON rather than leaving it only in the script.

SHORTLIST_SIZE.needs: shortlist size used for the headline numbers

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_SEARCH.needs: share of shortlist places going to male-named candidates under the search step alone, all categories

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_RANKER.needs: same, under the ranking model alone

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE.needs: same, under the two steps combined

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE; generated automatically

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_PIPELINE_NEUTRAL.needs: combined-pipeline shortlist share male, evenly split occupations only

SHORTLIST_PCT_MALE_SEARCH_FEMJOBS.needs: search step alone, female-typed occupations (REVIEW_TODO A6: describe as leaning in the opposite direction, never as `fairer`)

FF_MALE_RATE.needs: derived four-fifths arithmetic (REVIEW_TODO A12): selection rate of the male-named half of the pool = (share of shortlist that is male x shortlist size) / (pool size / 2)

FF_FEMALE_RATE.needs: derived: selection rate of the female-named half of the pool

FF_SELECTION_RATIO.needs: derived: impact ratio, female selection rate divided by male selection rate; compared against the 0.80 four-fifths benchmark

FF_SELECTION_RATIO_GLOSS.needs: plain-English gloss of FF_SELECTION_RATIO, e.g. `about a quarter`; generated automatically

DEID_ORIGINAL_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS.needs: SCHEMA CHANGE PENDING. Share favoring the man on male-typed jobs, untransformed documents, as a PERCENTAGE 0-100 under `conditions.<name>.by_category.<category>.pct_male` (matching the convention already used by analyze_single_stage.py and compounding_experiment.py).

DEID_NAMESONLY_PCT_MALE_MALEJOBS.needs: SCHEMA CHANGE PENDING. Same, names-only condition (REVIEW_TODO A4: direction becomes near-deterministic while magnitude falls).

DEID_ORIGINAL_MEAN_GAP.needs: average absolute score gap between the twins, untransformed, on this model's own scale

DEID_NAMESONLY_MEAN_GAP.needs: average absolute score gap, names-only condition; must be SMALLER than DEID_ORIGINAL_MEAN_GAP (REVIEW_TODO A4)

UTILITY_TOP1_AFTER.needs: NOT YET PRODUCED. Same after the full de-identification transform. Legally load-bearing: a less discriminatory alternative must be equally effective.

TABLE_MODELS.needs: tabular-only fragment: model, vendor/access, n, score range, tie %, date scored (REVIEW_TODO B7)

TABLE_SINGLE_STAGE.needs: tabular-only fragment: per model and category, % male / % tie / % female plus tie-aware % with cluster-bootstrap CI (REVIEW_TODO A2, B1)

TABLE_CONSISTENCY.needs: tabular-only fragment: per model, k of N occupations leaning each way (REVIEW_TODO B1)

TABLE_ROBUST_TEMPLATE.needs: tabular-only fragment: tie-aware % male-favoured by document template (REVIEW_TODO B2)

TABLE_ROBUST_QUERY.needs: tabular-only fragment: tie-aware % male-favoured by query phrasing (REVIEW_TODO B2)

TABLE_ROBUST_NAMEPAIR.needs: tabular-only fragment: tie-aware % male-favoured by name pair (REVIEW_TODO B2, A4)

TABLE_SWEEP.needs: tabular-only fragment: pipeline shortlist share male for every ranking model behind the same search step (REVIEW_TODO B5)

TABLE_DEID.needs: NOT YET PRODUCED. Tabular-only fragment from deidentification_experiment.py: one row per condition (original, names_only, pronouns_only, full, gram_her_their, gram_her_them, gram_pos) with % favouring the man, % tied, and mean absolute score gap (REVIEW_TODO A4, A5, A10).

DEID_GRAM_NAIVE_PCT_RESIDUE.needs: Share of twin pairs the NAIVE grammatical mapping (her->their regardless of part of speech) leaves textually different (REVIEW_TODO A5). The POS-aware variant gram_pos leaves 0%.
